title: Expressing the Radius of a Tangent Circle in Terms of Distance a and Angle theta
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: In the given geometric configuration, a ray from a vertex makes an acute angle \theta with a horizontal tangent line to a circle of radius r. The ray passes through the center of the circle, and the portion of the ray outside the circle from the vertex to the circle's circumference has length a. Express the radius r of the circle in terms of a and \theta.

steps.title: Form a Right Triangle Using the Circle's Center and Point of Tangency
steps.explanation: Draw the vertical radius of length r from the center of the circle to the point of tangency on the horizontal base. Since a tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, this forms a right triangle with angle theta, opposite vertical leg r, and hypotenuse of total length a + r.
steps.why: The distance from the vertex to the center equals the external segment a plus the radius r.

steps.title: Write the Sine Ratio for Angle theta
steps.explanation: In this right triangle, sin(theta) is the ratio of the vertical radius r to the hypotenuse a + r.
steps.why: By definition of sine in a right triangle, sin(theta) = opposite / hypotenuse.

steps.title: Solve the Algebraic Equation for r
steps.explanation: Multiply both sides by a + r, expand the left side, collect all terms containing r on the right side, and divide by 1 - sin(theta).
steps.why: Linear isolation of r yields r = (a*sin(theta))/(1 - sin(theta)).
